items.title: Steam Game Reviews Stretch to 12 Business Days: Valve Tightens Checklist to Stop Untested Submissions
items.summary: Build reviews for developers releasing games on Steam are running late. Valve acknowledged surging submissions and frequent repeat reviews, revising its checklist to cover launch testing and cloud saves as reviews targeting three to five days now sometimes take up to 12 business days.

items.title: Microsoft reissues Excel KB5002934 to fix copy-and-paste regression
items.summary: Microsoft has reissued Excel 2016 security update KB5002934 as build 16.0.5574.1006 to fix a copy-and-paste failure in the earlier release. An October Patch Tuesday forecast had flagged the Excel problem for a fix, but the October update brought it back for some users. Source

items.title: Google will cut off school Search accounts that reject its AI
items.summary: Starting early next year, K–12 schools that keep Google’s AI features disabled will also lose Google Search for student accounts. Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search will be off until school administrators enable them, leaving schools without a Search-only option if they reject Google’s AI. Source

items.title: Windows 11’s new memory work keeps up to 2 GB more data in RAM
items.summary: Microsoft says Windows 11 can now keep up to 2 GB more active data in memory on 8 GB PCs, and a demanding multitasking test ran up to 40% faster. The figures add detail to its earlier claims of improved responsiveness and memory savings for low-RAM systems. Source

items.title: Agentic AI helped build Windows 11’s Quick Settings speed test in a day
items.summary: Windows 11’s Quick Settings speed test checks ping, download, and upload speeds without opening a browser. Microsoft says an agentic AI workflow, guided by one person in spare time, helped turn the idea into a working prototype in a day.

items.title: Revolut cuts AI coding costs 90% with self-hosted GLM
items.summary: Revolut is a UK-based financial technology company offering banking, payments and other financial services through its app. The company cut AI coding costs by about 90% after making self-hosted the Chinese GLM models the default for roughly 2,000 engineers.

items.title: Fake software installers quietly turn Windows PCs into proxy and compute nodes

items.title: Cryptographic Proof That an AI Answer Came From the Specified Model: Anthropic Releases FlashProve
items.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, a system that cryptographically verifies that an AI inference result came from a specified model. Proofs are about 19MB and require 70–95 times the GPU compute time of ordinary inference; this is a research artifact with no planned service deployment.

items.title: Open-source file sync tool rsync 3.5.2 fixes a CPU exhaustion flaw
items.summary: The rsync project released version 3.5.2, and it closes a flaw that let a connecting client tie up a server’s CPU with checksum math that leads nowhere. The new version also lets you push a transfer to the back of the queue for CPU and disk, so a big sync stops elbowing everything else on the machine.

items.title: Candidate and Active Configuration on IOS XR
items.summary: Traditional network devices used a single (active or running) configuration, with a snapshot of it stored in permanent memory (startup configuration). The active configuration was modified with every configuration command, making it a perfect recipe for disaster in the days of in-band configuration 1 .

items.title: Ghostunnel: Open-source TLS proxy with mutual authentication
items.summary: Ghostunnel is an open-source proxy that handles TLS for programs that cannot handle it themselves. It works in two directions. In server mode it sits in front of a backend, accepts TLS connections, checks the client’s certificate, then passes traffic to the service behind it over TCP or a UNIX socket.
